cards.title: Stealth Renewal Risk at Helios Robotics
cards.synthesis: Helios Robotics renews in 103 days and the executive layer just got reset. The prior champion Nora Vargas has departed and the new VP Engineering, Lena Ferreira, has openly told us she's evaluating Slack and other options before signing. Health score (82) and call sentiment look fine on the surface, but $1.04M in ARR is sitting on a relationship we no longer have. We need a senior touch into Lena before this becomes a competitive bake-off we didn't know we were in.

recommended_action.what: Have Sarah personally request an executive-to-executive introduction with Lena Ferreira this week, paired with a tailored value review ahead of the renewal cycle.

evidence.claim: Contract renewal in 103 days (2026-08-30), placing account in imminent renewal window.
Previous sponsor Nora Vargas has departed the organization; new VP Engineering Lena Ferreira has assumed decision authority.

New executive sponsor (Lena Ferreira) recently introduced and is openly evaluating alternative vendors before renewal; competitor (Slack) explicitly mentioned in context of vendor consolidation review.
New sponsor previously used competing product and is actively reviewing options, suggesting lack of established relationship and competitive exposure.
CS notes flag relationship transition as a risk, with new sponsor conducting vendor evaluation before renewal.

cards.title: Two Realities at Solstice Hospitality
cards.synthesis: Solstice Hospitality is our largest account in this briefing at $1.44M ARR, and we're telling ourselves two completely different stories about it. Sales and CS calls describe 'steady adoption' through March, while Support has logged 8 bug tickets with sentiment crashing to -0.84, the executive sponsor has gone silent after a reorg, and admin console usage has dropped 39% with docs down 26%. Customers are explicitly invoking renewal in ticket language. The health score of 83 is hiding all of it — and Owen, the CSM, has authored both the optimistic notes and the risk flags without anyone reconciling them.

recommended_action.what: Convene a one-hour account reset between CSM, AE, and Support Lead this week to align on a single Solstice narrative and a 30-day stabilization plan before the next sponsor touch.

evidence.claim: March 4 call summarizes 'steady adoption' and positive sentiment; February 28 call documents customer frustration with admin console reliability and mixed sentiment.

13 tickets in last 90 days with 8 categorized as bugs; 5 high/critical severity bugs (tkt_00486, tkt_00487, tkt_00488, tkt_00489, tkt_00490) explicitly mention repeated failures and frustration; negative sentiment scores cluster -0.47 to -0.84.
Core features showing significant decline: admin_console -39.4%, docs -26.0%, meetings -20.8%, search -22.4%; chat and calendar up, but overall productivity features trending down.
Risk-category notes (csn_00175, csn_00176, csn_00177) from Jan–Mar flag sponsor unreachability, declining core workflow usage, and eroding trust from repeated admin console issues.
Support and Solutions Engineer both raised risk signals (sig_00062, sig_00063) in March flagging sharp tone shift in tickets and unreliable admin console affecting multiple accounts.
Health score 83 suggests overall positive account status, masking the underlying deterioration in support sentiment, usage, and engagement.

cards.title: Admin Console Reliability Is a Portfolio-Level Threat
cards.synthesis: Admin console reliability is no longer an account issue — it's a portfolio issue touching 14 accounts and $12.6M in ARR. Eleven accounts have filed bugs on reports not matching actual usage, eight on role updates taking over 30 minutes to propagate, and six on missing logs and empty CSV exports. Seven accounts now show admin console usage down more than 20%, and the language in tickets is sharp: customers from Horizon, Solstice, and Onyx are all linking these failures to their renewal conversations. This needs to land in front of Engineering before the next sprint planning.

recommended_action.what: Package the admin console evidence into an engineering escalation brief and get it onto next week's product leadership agenda, with a parallel proactive comms note from CS to the affected accounts.

evidence.claim: 11 distinct accounts filed bugs on 'Admin console reports do not match underlying usage' with negative sentiment ranging from -0.24 to -0.83
8 distinct accounts filed bugs on 'Admin console role updates take >30 minutes to propagate' with consistent negative sentiment (-0.20 to -0.84)
6 distinct accounts filed bugs on 'Admin console logs missing entries for the last 48h' and 'Admin console exports return empty CSV files'
7 accounts showing significant admin_console feature usage decline (>20%): acc_005, acc_006, acc_015, acc_019, acc_020, acc_024, acc_025
9 distinct accounts filed bugs on 'Documents intermittently fail to load on first open' and 'Mobile app crashes when opening large spreadsheets' with highly negative sentiment (-0.19 to -0.64)
10 distinct accounts filed bugs on 'Workflow trigger fires twice for the same event' with consistent negative sentiment (-0.12 to -0.64)
8 distinct accounts filed bugs on 'Search results miss documents shared in the last week' with highly negative sentiment (-0.23 to -0.83)
5 accounts showing significant docs feature usage decline correlating with document loading complaints

cards.title: We're Building What Customers Aren't Asking For
cards.synthesis: Granular permissions is the single most-requested capability across your portfolio — 26 call mentions and 29 ticket requests across 20 accounts representing $12.9M ARR — and it's nowhere on the roadmap. Meanwhile AI meeting summaries is in-progress with significant investment despite only two tickets and almost no call demand. This is a fixable misallocation, but it requires you to bring the portfolio evidence into the product prioritization conversation before the next planning cycle locks in.

recommended_action.what: Bring the granular permissions demand evidence to the next product roadmap review and propose reallocating capacity from AI meeting summaries toward a permissions workstream for Q3.

evidence.claim: Granular permissions and permissions model topics mentioned 26 times combined (10 + 8 + 8) in customer calls over 180 days, indicating sustained high demand.
29 of 38 feature-request tickets (76%) explicitly request granular permissions in various forms (per-row, per-folder, workspace-level, external collaborators), across 20 distinct accounts.
No roadmap item exists for granular permissions capability despite being the highest-demand feature by convergent signal (call mentions + ticket volume).
support_refs: rm_001 through rm_015: no permissions feature

evidence.claim: AI meeting summaries (rm_001) has high investment level and in_progress status, but only 2 feature-request tickets and low call demand (implied from topic list).

API usage and integration scoping topics mentioned 12 times each, suggesting demand for deeper integration/API access capabilities, partially reflected in feature-request tickets for API access to IdP integrations.

cards.title: Expansion Window Open at Quartz Semiconductors
cards.synthesis: Quartz Semiconductors is quietly expanding under its own steam. Search usage is up 48%, admin console up 30%, and Finance, Legal, and Ops have all started showing up in the last quarter with sophisticated questions on SSO custom IdPs, programmatic admin reporting, and webhook reliability. The CSM has already noted an expansion conversation that hasn't happened yet, and with renewal four months out at a healthy 92 score, the timing is ideal to convert this organic growth into a commercial conversation before it gets entangled with the renewal.

recommended_action.what: Have the AE draft and present an expansion proposal to Mateo Iyer within the next two weeks, anchored on the new Finance/Legal/Ops adoption.

evidence.claim: Broad usage acceleration across multiple features in last 60 days: search +48.0%, admin_console +29.9%, mobile_app +22.1%, meetings +14.2%, docs +9.1%, chat +7.4%, shared_drive +7.1%.

Most recent call (2026-05-17, call_00159) notes Finance, Legal, and Ops adoption over last quarter with sophisticated questions on API limits and SSO configuration; sentiment positive; action item to draft expansion proposal drafted but no commercial conversation initiated yet.

CS note from 2026-04-12 (csn_00162) explicitly flags new users from Finance/Legal/Ops, sophisticated API/SSO questions, and opportunity for commercial expansion conversation that has not yet occurred.
Signal sig_00055 (2026-05-10) identifies new activations from Finance/Legal/Ops in last 8 weeks as clear cross-departmental expansion in motion.

Recent tickets show power-user behavior: SSO custom IdP configuration (tkt_00433), programmatic admin reporting feature request (tkt_00434), webhook reliability for procurement workflow (tkt_00432) — all advanced use cases.
Executive sponsor (Mateo Iyer, CIO) last logged in 2026-05-17 (2 days before reference date); account health_score 92; contract extends to 2026-09-15 (4 months out).
